title: Attention Bottleneck
definition: The process of a large language model focusing on and extracting the main concept or idea from a large amount of text, reducing the number of detailed insights.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Think of a large language model like Mistral as a super-focused reader. It reads a lot of text but only remembers the most important ideas. This makes it good at summarizing.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: The attention bottleneck refers to the fact that large language models, when processing large amounts of text, often distill the main idea and compress the information, neglecting some detailed insights.
difficulty_levels.expert: The attention bottleneck is a result of the transformer architecture used in large language models, which employs self-attention mechanisms. This architecture allows the model to focus on certain parts of the text while disregarding others, a process akin to selective memory. This feature is both a strength and a limitation, enabling efficient processing of large amounts of text but potentially causing the model to overlook or misinterpret some nuanced details.

extra_fields.insight: Mistral's ability to consistently extract 1-2 core concepts per 1,000 words suggests a natural attention bottleneck in large language models.
